raw_response: {"translations":[{"id":"T0271","english":"The environment does not support using the desklamp as an examine tool argument, nor bare names or compound syntax; examining furniture does not provide valid information, the put action itself does not trigger the observation success condition, and some furniture may refuse placement."},{"id":"T0272","english":"After locating the target object and bringing it to the furniture where the desklamp is, use the observed numbered instance to execute use desklamp <id>. Do not use examine X with desklamp, examine target/desklamp/furniture, or compound use syntax; after invalid syntax, verify the desklamp instance name and retry rather than repeatedly examining. If put to that furniture repeatedly produces no change, keep holding it and directly use desklamp <id>."},{"id":"T0273","english":"When use desklamp produces no change, first verify position, instance name, and held state"},{"id":"T0274","english":"If use desklamp returns Nothing happens, it usually means you are not at the location of the desklamp, the current furniture observation does not list a desklamp, you used a bare name rather than a numbered instance, or the target object has not been obtained and interaction conditions are not met; repeating the same use/examine/look at the same location will not change state, and after one or two consecutive failures you should stop repeating to avoid loops or protection. If the target object cannot be placed on the furniture where the desklamp is, and put repeatedly produces no change, you should also not continue placing."},{"id":"T0275","english":"Using the desklamp requires being at the same location as the furniture where the desklamp is, and satisfying conditions such as the instance name and holding the target object; wrong syntax, wrong location, or not holding the target object will not produce a state change, and an empty observation is not a retry signal. The put action itself does not trigger the observation condition."},{"id":"T0276","english":"After failure, first verify whether the current furniture observation lists desklamp; if not, move to other furniture that lists a desklamp rather than retrying the same use. When the desklamp is present, confirm the target object has been obtained or is being held, and retry with the numbered use desklamp <id>; if there is still no change, search other locations or declare inability to complete, do not repeat the same command or fall back to examine. If put repeatedly produces no change, stop placing and keep holding it to directly use the desklamp."},{"id":"T0277","english":"Desklamp observation search: prioritize open surfaces, then systematically check containers"},{"id":"T0278","english":"When searching for the target object or desklamp, prioritize checking open surfaces related to the desklamp, such as desk, sidetable, nightstand, bed, dresser, sofa, coffeetable, armchair, shelf, etc.; once a desklamp is observed, go directly to the furniture where it is and use the desklamp if needed, without continuing to traverse many drawers or unrelated containers. If the target object is not found on reasonable open surfaces, then systematically search by container type (drawer/cabinet), and return to the desklamp after finding it. Avoid repeatedly look/examine at the same location; when there is no new information, turn to other furniture or containers. 'under the desklamp' does not guarantee that the target object or desklamp is at the assumed location; when the assumed location is not visible, search other surfaces and containers, and if the desklamp is actually on other furniture, go to that furniture rather than repeatedly checking the original location."},{"id":"T0279","english":"In the desklamp observation task, when searching for the target object or desklamp, or when you have arrived at the assumed desklamp location but the target object/desklamp is not there and consecutive observations yield no new information."},{"id":"T0280","english":"When the goal is to heat first and then place: locate and take the target object; if it is already in hand, proceed directly to heating; go to the microwave, open it if closed; complete heating in a way confirmed feasible by observation; keep tracking the same object instance. Heating is only an intermediate milestone; the task is complete only after the object has been placed at the destination. After heating, if the object was actually put into the microwave, take it out; if heating was completed while holding it, keep holding it and go directly to the destination. Go to the final destination, open the container if necessary, put the object in, and confirm placement. Do not treat successful heating as task completion, and do not needlessly restart already completed acquisition steps."},{"id":"T0281","english":"When the task requires first heating the object, then placing it at the specified destination."},{"id":"T0282","english":"Explicit commands for microwave heating and state-switch recovery"},{"id":"T0283","english":"Before using the microwave, open it first and confirm via observation that it is open. Prefer a heating form that explicitly specifies the object and microwave, such as heat <object> with microwave <id>; generic forms such as bare use <object> or use microwave may return Nothing happens. During heating the object may be held or placed in the opened microwave; confirm the actual state according to the current observation. If held heating returns Nothing happens, you may put the object into the opened microwave and retry; if the attempt inside the microwave fails, take the object out, confirm the microwave is open, and switch to holding it to retry; you may also try holding it again after putting it in and taking it back out. After the first failure, change the object's position or held state; do not repeat the exact same failed command; if there is still no confirmation after switching, you may switch between the two states once more. Only after observing explicit heating success should you continue to the destination."},{"id":"T0284","english":"Do not continue placing without confirmed heating success"},{"id":"T0285","english":"The heating command may fail or return Nothing happens; treating an unconfirmed attempt as success may cause you to move and place an object that is still cold. You cannot infer heating success merely because the object is held or placed in the microwave. When observation only shows the microwave is open or the object is still held, you also cannot judge that it has been placed or heated."}]}
